_about: Numbers and exact statements that the condensed note (GFF/note/long_range_ising_condensed.tex, edition fa71533 of 13 October 2026) quotes for the d=3 power-sector compensation of C6(3) and the d=3 finite-scheme inputs, and that the research-bundle package lri_C6_d3_complete_update produces. Sections: 'Analytic power-sector compensation at d=2,3' (subsections 'Power subgraphs: a separate three-dimensional audit', 'An exact cancellation avoids two unknown core integrals', 'Assembled power correction and completeness') and 'Finite-scheme sixth-order assembly' (subsections 'The changes required by dimension three', 'Regulator dependence and finite-order extraction'). The C6(3) production (GFF/code/LRI_C6_D3_HPC) uses this retained analytic compensation and does not redo it. Read by code/lri_C6_d3_complete_update/public/replay.py. Written by Claude (session C63d) on 2026-10-13 for the public release; the values were produced on 14 September 2026 in the research conversation that made the bundle.

sunset.note_says: M_3 = -16 pi/15; each of L6G106, L6G117 contributes -4 M_3 P_4(3) to b_6 and zero to c_6

coverage.note_says: 1, 5, 31 relevant power-containing classes at loops 3, 4, 5; at six loops all 121 power classes with 3w_B - w_A != 0 are included, the other 52 have zero weight; 660 sixth-order classes, 487 power-free and 173 with a proper power subgraph; 1, 5, 16, 76, 395 nonzero power-free kernels at L = 2..6; two non-power four-loop graphs rejected by the coordinate reduction are supplied by the finite-kernel integration

core.note_says: Substituting (u0,u1) = (0,0) and (101,-37) in the full graph recursion changes the three individual residues exactly as predicted, to better than 4e-73.
core.tolerance: exact (SymPy) for the identities; 1e-70 for the numeric jets at 75 working digits; the stated bound for the trial residues

lower_power.tolerance: exact (SymPy) in power_assembly_polynomial.json; 1e-60 numerically against the graph recursion

power_correction.note_says: At 90 working digits the two parts, including the factor 1/2187, are +-0.0736516970441648694692229455611...; their sum is -1.02e-89. A separate 75-digit run with different core assignments gives -1.94e-75. A third algebraic stress test with Q=7, P=11, K=5, Z=13 and core (-17,29) gives 1.52e-65 at 65 working digits.
power_correction.tolerance: higher/lower: one unit in the 31st decimal shown; sums: the recorded value rounded to three significant digits equals the note

gamma_jets.note_says: All 20 Gamma logarithmic jets and five normalizations were freshly checked by independent 65-digit Cauchy evaluation of the analytic Gamma product. The maximum absolute discrepancy is 2.27e-59.
gamma_jets.tolerance: count exact; the maximum rounds to the shown three digits

two_loop.note_says: beta jets through z^4; two fresh 60-digit evaluations use radii 0.05, 0.07 and respectively 48, 64 Cauchy nodes
two_loop.tolerance: one unit in the last shown digit (16 decimals); the two radii agree to 1e-50

lagrange.note_says: An independent rational-polynomial implementation of implicit fixed-point substitution and bivariate Lagrange inversion gives 256 exact checks, including 32 checks of the constant-MS sixth-order assembly.

master_inputs.note_says: The audit uses Q_3 and P_4(3) as common inputs; their values are those of the section 'Three dimensions' (33 decimals shown there). The code carries 38 to 39 decimals as defaults.
master_inputs.tolerance: one unit in the last shown digit
